title: Review
summary: Review day for the OOP module: classes and instances, getters and setters with @property, class vs instance data, the three method types, inheritance, composition and polymorphism. The curriculum has no separate review page; its OOP module page says Assessment #1 comes at the end of the week, so confirm the date and rules in #eagle. Step-by-step guide arrives when the lecture is published.
goal: Explain and use every OOP idea from the week without notes.

steps.title: Re-read the OOP module pages
steps.detail: Skim the three OOP lessons (Intro, Abstraction and Encapsulation, Inheritance and Polymorphism). Write one line plus one tiny example per idea in a topic note in notes/topics/.
steps.doneWhen: Your note covers encapsulation, abstraction, inheritance, polymorphism and composition, each with an example.

steps.title: Get quizzed by the tutor
steps.detail: Use the tutor agent from the workspace root to find gaps. It asks questions; you answer before it explains.
steps.code: Use the tutor agent to quiz me on Python OOP: class vs instance attributes, @property getters and setters, @classmethod vs @staticmethod, super(), composition vs inheritance, and polymorphism. One question at a time, and don't tell me the answer until I've tried.
steps.doneWhen: You answered at least 8 questions and wrote down the ones you missed.

steps.title: Confirm the assessment rules
steps.detail: Ask in #eagle_questions when Assessment #1 is, what format it takes, and which resources (including AI) are allowed. Follow those rules exactly.
steps.doneWhen: You know the assessment date, format and allowed resources.

steps.title: Close out the week's OOP assignments
steps.detail: Check progress.md for any OOP 2 or OOP 3 assignments still open and push what you have with /save-project.
steps.doneWhen: Every OOP assignment row in progress.md is up to date.

concepts.meaning: Keeping an object's data behind methods (like getters and setters) so it can't be changed carelessly.
Showing only what a user of the class needs and hiding the details.
A child class reuses and extends a parent class.
Same method name, different behavior depending on the object.
An object built from other objects it holds, instead of inheriting from them.
